convention: Planetocentric latitude (deg, N+), east-positive longitude (-180..180). Matches the map (Leaflet EPSG4326, [lat, lng]).

status_legend.in_handoff: Value comes from the Developer 2 handoff (cites Bell et al. 2023).
status_legend.recalled: Written from memory of NASA/JPL/PDS public information; NOT re-verified in this build (no internet). Check the source before publishing.

sites.name: Jezero Crater
sites.summary: Ancient lake basin with a river delta; Mars 2020 Perseverance landing site.
hazards: Rocky, steep delta and crater-rim terrain
No site-specific dust, temperature or radiation measurements are bundled
sites.data: Real CTX DEM (20 m/px) and orthomosaic are linked in datasets/jezero; rasters are not bundled.

sites.name: Gale Crater
sites.summary: Crater with a ~5 km layered mound (Aeolis Mons); Curiosity (MSL) landing site.
hazards: Sand ripples and sharp rocks damaged rover wheels
sites.data: MSL RAD and REMS surface measurements exist on NASA PDS; not bundled.

sites.name: Arcadia Planitia
sites.summary: Smooth northern lowland; orbital data suggest shallow buried ice at mid-latitudes.
hazards: Ice depth and amount need dedicated radar/neutron data
sites.data: Use Mars Odyssey GRS and SHARAD radar products from PDS; not bundled. Map marker is an approximate region centre: verify in the USGS Gazetteer.

sites.name: Elysium Planitia
sites.summary: Flat equatorial plain; InSight lander site.
sites.data: InSight weather and seismic data are on PDS; not bundled.

environment.text: MSL RAD measured about 0.64 mSv/day (galactic cosmic rays) at Gale Crater's surface (Hassler et al., 2014, Science 343:1244797).
Mostly CO2, surface pressure under 1% of Earth's: unbreathable, and too thin for stable liquid water at most places.
Regional and occasional global dust storms occur; the 2018 global storm ended Opportunity's mission.
Phoenix (2008) uncovered ice near 68 N; Mars Odyssey GRS maps hydrogen-rich shallow soil toward the poles.
